scope: Twelve original teaching examples, the original connected account, twelve analysis tasks, and full verbal display routes. No ordered graded-answer sequence is reproduced.

findings.observation: Case, agreement and hear+accusative support the intended participants.

findings.text: Ðā hīerde se munuc ðone sang.
findings.observation: Adverb-first finite/nominal-subject order is a supported tendency.

findings.text: Ðā hē ðone sang hīerde, ðā ēode hē tō ðǣm bisceope.
findings.observation: Temporal conjunction and correlative adverb are distinct; known gān/tō frame.

findings.text: Se sang wæs swēte. Hē wæs ēac wynsum.
findings.observation: Masculine sang supports hē while English renders it; no gender-only universal rule.

findings.text: Se bisceop geseah ðone munuc and grētte hine.
findings.observation: The expressed subject continues through coordination; grētan actual earlier sense explicitly includes greet.

findings.text: Se bisceop geseah ðone munuc. Hē wæs on ðǣm hūse.
findings.observation: Both masculine referents remain possible without more context; ambiguity is intentional.

findings.text: Se bisceop cwæð: “Ic wille mid ēow sprecan.”
findings.observation: New sprecan INF pair and explicit conversation mid+dative frame resolve earlier citation/sense gaps.

findings.text: Se munuc, ðe se bisceop grētte, ēode tō ðǣre cirican.
findings.observation: Relative internal object differs from nominative antecedent; source nominal audit owns cirican.

findings.text: Ðā se bisceop cōm, ðā sungon ðā brōðor.
findings.observation: Three ðā tokens have distinct conjunction/adverb/article roles.

findings.text: Se bisceop wæs on ðǣm hūse, and se munuc on ðǣre cirican.
findings.observation: Bounded repeated-predicate ellipsis is corroborated by Cook134 and prior Unit10.

findings.text: Hē sægde ðæt se sang swēte wǣre.
findings.observation: Known indirect report and past subjunctive; relative reporting time, not absolute past by form alone.

Coherent hearing, question, summons and assembly. lǣd requires the new complete command pair and person+direction frame; sprecan requires its complete INF pair and conversation frame; ðǣr and ęft require explicit promotion/new sense. Final word is a new source-owned complete nominal system. No obedience sense is inferred from hearing.
Checked vocabulary, finite morphology, case/antecedent roles and stated context; no extra ordering or reference rule is required.
